questions.problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)={x}_{1}(t)+4 \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=-{x}_{1}(t)+3{x}_{2}(t)-2,\end{aligned}\,x(0)=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the initial value problem above. By applying the Laplace transform to both sides of each equation, we get the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}{{field-1}}={X}_{1}(s)+{{field-2}} \\ s{X}_{2}(s)+1=-{X}_{1}(s)+3{X}_{2}(s)-{{field-3}}\end{aligned}
$$

where ${X}_{1}(s)=L{{x}_{1}(t)}$ and ${X}_{2}(s)=L{{x}_{2}(t)}$ are the Laplace transforms of the functions ${x}_{1}(t)$ and ${x}_{2}(t),$ respectively.
questions.worked_solution:
First, we compute the Laplace transforms of both sides of each equation in our system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}L{{x}_{1}^{′}(t)}=L{{x}_{1}(t)+4} \\ L{{x}_{2}^{′}(t)}=L{-{x}_{1}(t)+3{x}_{2}(t)-2}\end{aligned}\,\,
$$

Using the derivative property of the Laplace transform, we obtain the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}sL{{x}_{1}(t)}-{x}_{1}(0)=L{{x}_{1}(t)}+4L{1} \\ sL{{x}_{2}(t)}-{x}_{2}(0)=-L{{x}_{1}(t)}+3L{{x}_{2}(t)}-2L{1}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the result

$$
L{1}=\frac{1}{s},
$$

 we can write our system as follows:

$$
{\begin{aligned}s{X}_{1}(s)-1={X}_{1}(s)+\frac{4}{s} \\ s{X}_{2}(s)+1=-{X}_{1}(s)+3{X}_{2}(s)-\frac{2}{s}\end{aligned}
$$

where ${X}_{1}(s)=L{{x}_{1}(t)}$ and ${X}_{2}(s)=L{{x}_{2}(t)}$ are the Laplace transforms of the functions ${x}_{1}(t)$ and ${x}_{2}(t),$ respectively.

questions.problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=2{x}_{1}(t)+3{x}_{2}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=5{x}_{2}(t)+2,\end{aligned}\,x(0)=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the initial value problem above. By applying the Laplace transform $L$ to both sides of each equation in our system, we get a system with variables ${X}_{1}(s)=L{{x}_{1}(t)}$ and ${X}_{2}(s)=L{{x}_{2}(t)}.$ In terms of the parameter $s,$ the solution of the new system is

${X}_{1}(s)=$ {{field-1}},$\,$
${X}_{2}(s)=\frac{s+2}{s(s-5)}.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we compute the Laplace transforms of both sides of each equation in our system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}L{{x}_{1}^{′}(t)}=L{2{x}_{1}(t)+3{x}_{2}(t)} \\ L{{x}_{2}^{′}(t)}=L{5{x}_{2}(t)+2}\end{aligned}\,\,
$$

Using the derivative property of the Laplace transform, we obtain the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}sL{{x}_{1}(t)}-{x}_{1}(0)=2L{{x}_{1}(t)}+3L{{x}_{2}(t)} \\ sL{{x}_{2}(t)}-{x}_{2}(0)=5L{{x}_{2}(t)}+2L{1}\end{aligned}
$$

which can be simplified to the following:

$$
{\begin{aligned}s{X}_{1}(s)-0=2{X}_{1}(s)+3{X}_{2}(s) \\ s{X}_{2}(s)-1=5{X}_{2}(s)+\frac{2}{s}\end{aligned}
$$

where ${X}_{1}(s)=L{{x}_{1}(t)}$ and ${X}_{2}(s)=L{{x}_{2}(t)},$ and we have used the fact that $L{1}=\frac{1}{s}.$

Now, solving the second equation for ${X}_{2}(s),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}s{X}_{2}(s)-1 & =5{X}_{2}(s)+\frac{2}{s} \\ (s-5){X}_{2}(s) & =1+\frac{2}{s} \\ (s-5){X}_{2}(s) & =\frac{s+2}{s} \\ {X}_{2}(s) & =\frac{s+2}{s(s-5)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this in the first equation and solving for ${X}_{1}(s)$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}s{X}_{1}(s) & =2{X}_{1}(s)+3{X}_{2}(s) \\ (s-2){X}_{1}(s) & =3{X}_{2}(s) \\ (s-2){X}_{1}(s) & =3(\frac{s+2}{s(s-5)}) \\ {X}_{1}(s) & =\frac{3(s+2)}{s(s-5)(s-2)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution of the new system in terms of parameter $s$ is 

$$
{X}_{1}(s)=\frac{3(s+2)}{s(s-2)(s-5)},\,{X}_{2}(s)=\frac{s+2}{s(s-5)}.
$$

questions.problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)={x}_{1}(t)+2{x}_{2}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=3{x}_{2}(t)+4,\end{aligned}\,x(0)=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the initial value problem above. By applying the Laplace transform $L$ to both sides of each equation in our system, we get a system with variables ${X}_{1}(s)=L{{x}_{1}(t)}$ and ${X}_{2}(s)=L{{x}_{2}(t)}.$ In terms of the parameter $s,$ the solution of the new system is

${X}_{1}(s)=$ {{field-1}} $,\,$
${X}_{2}(s)=\frac{2s+4}{s(s-3)}.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we compute the Laplace transforms of both sides of each equation in our system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}L{{x}_{1}^{′}(t)}=L{{x}_{1}(t)+2{x}_{2}(t)} \\ L{{x}_{2}^{′}(t)}=L{3{x}_{2}(t)+4}\end{aligned}\,\,
$$

Using the derivative property of the Laplace transform, we obtain the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}sL{{x}_{1}(t)}-{x}_{1}(0)=L{{x}_{1}(t)}+2L{{x}_{2}(t)} \\ sL{{x}_{2}(t)}-{x}_{2}(0)=3L{{x}_{2}(t)}+4L{1}\end{aligned}
$$

which can be simplified to the following:

$$
{\begin{aligned}s{X}_{1}(s)+1={X}_{1}(s)+2{X}_{2}(s) \\ s{X}_{2}(s)-2=3{X}_{2}(s)+\frac{4}{s}\end{aligned}
$$

where ${X}_{1}(s)=L{{x}_{1}(t)}$ and ${X}_{2}(s)=L{{x}_{2}(t)},$ and we have used the fact that $L{1}=\frac{1}{s}.$

Now, solving the second equation for ${X}_{2}(s),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}s{X}_{2}(s)-2 & =3{X}_{2}(s)+\frac{4}{s} \\ (s-3){X}_{2}(s) & =2+\frac{4}{s} \\ (s-3){X}_{2}(s) & =\frac{2s+4}{s} \\ {X}_{2}(s) & =\frac{2s+4}{s(s-3)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this in the first equation and solving for ${X}_{1}(s)$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}s{X}_{1}(s)+1 & ={X}_{1}(s)+2{X}_{2}(s) \\ (s-1){X}_{1}(s) & =2{X}_{2}(s)-1 \\ (s-1){X}_{1}(s) & =2(\frac{2s+4}{s(s-3)})-1 \\ (s-1){X}_{1}(s) & =\frac{4s+8}{s(s-3)}-1 \\ (s-1){X}_{1}(s) & =\frac{4s+8-s(s-3)}{s(s-3)} \\ (s-1){X}_{1}(s) & =\frac{4s+8-{s}^{2}+3s}{s(s-3)} \\ (s-1){X}_{1}(s) & =\frac{-{s}^{2}+7s+8}{s(s-3)} \\ {X}_{1}(s) & =\frac{-{s}^{2}+7s+8}{s(s-1)(s-3)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution of the new system in terms of parameter $s$ is 

$$
{X}_{1}(s)=\frac{-{s}^{2}+7s+8}{s(s-1)(s-3)},\,{X}_{2}(s)=\frac{2s+4}{s(s-3)}.
$$

$$

Consider the initial value problem above. By applying the Laplace transform $L$ to both sides of each equation in our system, we get a system with variables ${X}_{1}(s)=L{{x}_{1}(t)}$ and ${X}_{2}(s)=L{{x}_{2}(t)}.$ In terms of the parameter $s,$ the solution of the new system is

${X}_{1}(s)=\frac{s+5}{s(s+1)},\,$
${X}_{2}(s)=$ {{field-1}}.
questions.worked_solution:
First, we compute the Laplace transforms of both sides of each equation in our system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}L{{x}_{1}^{′}(t)}=L{-{x}_{1}(t)+5} \\ L{{x}_{2}^{′}(t)}=L{2{x}_{1}(t)+4{x}_{2}(t)}\end{aligned}\,\,
$$

Using the derivative property of the Laplace transform, we obtain the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}sL{{x}_{1}(t)}-{x}_{1}(0)=-L{{x}_{1}(t)}+5L{1} \\ sL{{x}_{2}(t)}-{x}_{2}(0)=2L{{x}_{1}(t)}+4L{{x}_{2}(t)}\end{aligned}
$$

which can be simplified to the following:

$$
{\begin{aligned}s{X}_{1}(s)-1=-{X}_{1}(s)+\frac{5}{s} \\ s{X}_{2}(s)+1=2{X}_{1}(s)+4{X}_{2}(s)\end{aligned}
$$

where ${X}_{1}(s)=L{{x}_{1}(t)}$ and ${X}_{2}(s)=L{{x}_{2}(t)},$ and we have used the fact that $L{1}=\frac{1}{s}.$

Now, solving the first equation for ${X}_{1}(s),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}s{X}_{1}(s)-1 & =-{X}_{1}(s)+\frac{5}{s} \\ (s+1){X}_{1}(s) & =1+\frac{5}{s} \\ (s+1){X}_{1}(s) & =\frac{s+5}{s} \\ {X}_{1}(s) & =\frac{s+5}{s(s+1)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this in the second equation and solving for ${X}_{2}(s),$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}s{X}_{2}(s)+1 & =2{X}_{1}(s)+4{X}_{2}(s) \\ (s-4){X}_{2}(s) & =2{X}_{1}(s)-1 \\ (s-4){X}_{2}(s) & =2(\frac{s+5}{s(s+1)})-1 \\ (s-4){X}_{2}(s) & =\frac{2(s+5)-s(s+1)}{s(s+1)} \\ (s-4){X}_{2}(s) & =\frac{-{s}^{2}+s+10}{s(s+1)} \\ {X}_{2}(s) & =\frac{-{s}^{2}+s+10}{s(s+1)(s-4)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution of the new system  in terms of parameter $s$ is 

$$
{X}_{1}(s)=\frac{s+5}{s(s+1)},\,{X}_{2}(s)=\frac{-{s}^{2}+s+10}{s(s+1)(s-4)}.
$$

First, we compute the Laplace transforms of both sides of each equation in our system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}L{{x}_{1}^{′}(t)}=L{-3{x}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}(t)} \\ L{{x}_{2}^{′}(t)}=L{4{x}_{2}(t)+6}\end{aligned}\,\,
$$

Using the derivative property of the Laplace transform, we obtain the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}sL{{x}_{1}(t)}-{x}_{1}(0)=-3L{{x}_{1}(t)}+L{{x}_{2}(t)} \\ sL{{x}_{2}(t)}-{x}_{2}(0)=4L{{x}_{2}(t)}+6L{1}\end{aligned}
$$

which can be simplified to the following:

$$
{\begin{aligned}s{X}_{1}(s)-2=-3{X}_{1}(s)+{X}_{2}(s) \\ s{X}_{2}(s)+1=4{X}_{2}(s)+\frac{6}{s}\end{aligned}
$$

where ${X}_{1}(s)=L{{x}_{1}(t)}$ and ${X}_{2}(s)=L{{x}_{2}(t)},$ and we have used the fact that $L{1}=\frac{1}{s}.$

Now, solving the second equation for ${X}_{2}(s),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}s{X}_{2}(s)+1 & =4{X}_{2}(s)+\frac{6}{s} \\ (s-4){X}_{2}(s) & =-1+\frac{6}{s} \\ (s-4){X}_{2}(s) & =\frac{-s+6}{s} \\ {X}_{2}(s) & =\frac{6-s}{s(s-4)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this in the first equation and solving for ${X}_{1}(s)$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}s{X}_{1}(s)-2 & =-3{X}_{1}(s)+{X}_{2}(s) \\ (s+3){X}_{1}(s) & =2+{X}_{2}(s) \\ (s+3){X}_{1}(s) & =2+(\frac{6-s}{s(s-4)}) \\ (s+3){X}_{1}(s) & =\frac{2s(s-4)+6-s}{s(s-4)} \\ (s+3){X}_{1}(s) & =\frac{2({s}^{2}-4s)+6-s}{s(s-4)} \\ (s+3){X}_{1}(s) & =\frac{2{s}^{2}-8s+6-s}{s(s-4)} \\ (s+3){X}_{1}(s) & =\frac{2{s}^{2}-9s+6}{s(s-4)} \\ {X}_{1}(s) & =\frac{2{s}^{2}-9s+6}{s(s-4)(s+3)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution of the new system in terms of parameter $s$ is 

$$
{X}_{1}(s)=\frac{2{s}^{2}-9s+6}{s(s-4)(s+3)},\,{X}_{2}(s)=\frac{6-s}{s(s-4)}.
$$

\begin{aligned}s{X}_{1}(s)-1 & =4{X}_{1}(s)+{X}_{2}(s) \\ (s-4){X}_{1}(s) & =1+{X}_{2}(s) \\ (s-4){X}_{1}(s) & =1+(\frac{2s+1}{s(s-3)}) \\ (s-4){X}_{1}(s) & =\frac{s(s-3)+2s+1}{s(s-3)} \\ (s-4){X}_{1}(s) & =\frac{{s}^{2}-3s+2s+1}{s(s-3)} \\ (s-4){X}_{1}(s) & =\frac{{s}^{2}-s+1}{s(s-3)} \\ {X}_{1}(s) & =\frac{{s}^{2}-s+1}{s(s-3)(s-4)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution of the new system in terms of parameter $s$ is 

$$
{X}_{1}(s)=\frac{{s}^{2}-s+1}{s(s-3)(s-4)},\,{X}_{2}(s)=\frac{2s+1}{s(s-3)}.
$$

$$

Consider the initial value problem above. By applying the Laplace transform to both sides of each equation in our system, we get a transformed system with the solution 

$$
{X}_{1}(s)=L{{x}_{1}(t)}=\frac{1}{s-1}-\frac{3}{s},\,{X}_{2}(s)=L{{x}_{2}(t)}=\frac{1/2}{s-1}-\frac{1}{s}+\frac{3/2}{s-3}.
$$

Find the solution to the original initial value problem.

To find ${x}_{1}(t)$ and ${x}_{2}(t)$ satisfying the original initial value problem, we apply the inverse Laplace transform to ${X}_{1}(s)$ and ${X}_{2}(s):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) & ={L}^{-1}{{X}_{1}(s)} \\  & ={L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s-1}-\frac{3}{s}} \\  & ={L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s-1}}-3{L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s}} \\  & ={e}^{1\cdot t}-3\cdot 1 \\  & ={e}^{t}-3 \\ {x}_{2}(t) & ={L}^{-1}{{X}_{2}(s)} \\  & ={L}^{-1}{\frac{1/2}{s-1}-\frac{1}{s}+\frac{3/2}{s-3}} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s-1}}-{L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s}}+\frac{3}{2}{L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s-3}} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{e}^{1\cdot t}-1+\frac{3}{2}{e}^{3\cdot t} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{e}^{t}+\frac{3}{2}{e}^{3t}-1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we write down the solution to the initial value problem:

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t}-3 \\ \frac{1}{2}{e}^{t}+\frac{3}{2}{e}^{3t}-1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14076259/assets/8161123eafa5ed80dc37b8e017c5598fcacaf241a84a09ca27f73d204d7b0e74.png)
Consider the initial value problem above. By applying the Laplace transform to both sides of each equation, find the system of equations.
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, we compute the Laplace transforms of both sides of each equation in our system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}L{{x}_{1}^{′}(t)}=L{2{x}_{1}(t)+5\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)-3} \\ L{{x}_{2}^{′}(t)}=L{-3{x}_{1}(t)+4{x}_{2}(t)+2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the derivative property of the Laplace transform, we obtain the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}sL{{x}_{1}(t)}-{x}_{1}(0)=2L{{x}_{1}(t)}+5L{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)}-3L{1} \\ sL{{x}_{2}(t)}-{x}_{2}(0)=-3L{{x}_{1}(t)}+4L{{x}_{2}(t)}+2L{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the results

$$
\mathcal L\{1\} = \dfrac{1}{s}, \quad
\mathcal L\{\cos(2t)\} = \dfrac{s}{s^2+4}, \quad
\mathcal L\{\sin(2t)\} = \dfrac{2}{s^2+4},
$$

we can write our system as follows:

$$
{\begin{aligned}s{X}_{1}(s)-1=2{X}_{1}(s)+\frac{5s}{{s}^{2}+4}-\frac{3}{s} \\ s{X}_{2}(s)+2=-3{X}_{1}(s)+4{X}_{2}(s)+\frac{4}{{s}^{2}+4}\end{aligned}
$$

where $X_1(s) = \mathcal{L}\left\{  x_1(t) \right\}$ and $X_2(s) = \mathcal{L}\left\{  x_2(t) \right\}$ are the Laplace transforms of the functions $x_1(t)$ and $x_2(t),$ respectively.

canonical_examples.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14076259/assets/ce973be1a5a98fa04fad06c1ca5ee19c7f1b0cfd421d0cd449c7cb52138bf9bd.png)
Consider the initial value problem above. By applying the Laplace transform $\mathcal{L}$ to both sides of each equation in our system, we get a system with variables $X_1(s) = \mathcal{L}\left\{  x_1(t) \right\}$ and $X_2(s) = \mathcal{L}\left\{  x_2(t) \right\}.$ In terms of the parameter $s,$  find the solution of the new system.
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, we compute the Laplace transforms of both sides of each equation in our system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}L{{x}_{1}^{′}(t)}=L{-{x}_{1}(t)+4} \\ L{{x}_{2}^{′}(t)}=L{2{x}_{1}(t)-3{x}_{2}(t)}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the derivative property of the Laplace transform, we obtain the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}sL{{x}_{1}(t)}-{x}_{1}(0)=-L{{x}_{1}(t)}+4L{1} \\ sL{{x}_{2}(t)}-{x}_{2}(0)=2L{{x}_{1}(t)}-3L{{x}_{2}(t)}\end{aligned}
$$

which can be simplified to the following:

$$
{\begin{aligned}s{X}_{1}(s)-1=-{X}_{1}(s)+\frac{4}{s} \\ s{X}_{2}(s)-0=2{X}_{1}(s)-3{X}_{2}(s)\end{aligned}
$$

where $X_1(s) = \mathcal{L}\left\{  x_1(t) \right\}$ and $X_2(s) = \mathcal{L}\left\{  x_2(t) \right\},$ and we have used the fact that $\mathcal L\{1\} = \dfrac1s.$

Now, solving the first equation for $X_1(s),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}s{X}_{1}(s)-1 & =-{X}_{1}(s)+\frac{4}{s} \\ (s+1){X}_{1}(s) & =1+\frac{4}{s} \\ (s+1){X}_{1}(s) & =\frac{s+4}{s} \\ {X}_{1}(s) & =\frac{s+4}{s(s+1)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this in the second equation and solving for $X_2(s),$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}s{X}_{2}(s) & =2{X}_{1}(s)-3{X}_{2}(s) \\ (s+3){X}_{2}(s) & =2{X}_{1}(s) \\ (s+3){X}_{2}(s) & =2(\frac{s+4}{s(s+1)}) \\ {X}_{2}(s) & =\frac{2(s+4)}{s(s+1)(s+3)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution of the new system in terms of parameter $s$ is 

$$
X_1(s) = \dfrac{s+4}{s(s+1)} ,\qquad 
X_2(s) = \dfrac{2(s+4)}{s(s+1)(s+3)}.
$$

$$

Find the solution to the original initial value problem.
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
To find $x_1(t)$ and $x_2(t)$ satisfying the original initial value problem, we apply the inverse Laplace transform to $X_1(s)$ and $X_2(s){:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) & ={L}^{-1}{{X}_{1}(s)} \\  & ={L}^{-1}{-\frac{1}{s+2}+\frac{2}{s-1}-\frac{2}{s}} \\  & =-{L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s+2}}+2\,{L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s-1}}-2\,{L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s}} \\  & =-{e}^{-2\cdot t}+2{e}^{1\cdot t}-2\cdot 1 \\  & =2{e}^{t}-{e}^{-2t}-2 \\ {x}_{2}(t) & ={L}^{-1}{{X}_{2}(s)} \\  & ={L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s+2}+\frac{3}{s}} \\  & ={L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s+2}}+3\,{L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s}} \\  & ={e}^{-2\cdot t}+3\cdot 1 \\  & ={e}^{-2t}+3\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we write down the solution to the initial value problem:

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2{e}^{t}-{e}^{-2t}-2 \\ {e}^{-2t}+3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
